operation_role_meanings.destination: The target location into which the operation writes, such as an upload directory.
operation_role_meanings.identifier_input: A name or locator selecting a structural target, such as an SQL table/column name or a filepath used to locate a file for download. A userid or filepath stored as SQL data is not an SQL identifier.
operation_role_meanings.input_unspecified: The source establishes an input to this operation but does not resolve its more specific role. It is not a default for objects used elsewhere or for merely possible input use.
operation_role_meanings.resource: An existing facility used by the operation, such as a database, base directory or source file. This is a capability or access facility, not every previously available object: a received data payload whose fields are parsed has value_input. Classify the entity denoted by the concept: a facility can be named by a literal path without becoming a separate locator-value object. A caller-supplied path selecting a target has identifier_input instead. Do not substitute the operation's result for a resource.
operation_role_meanings.result: The operation produces or exposes the WHOLE object denoted by this exact source instance, including an existing object explicitly returned to the caller. Supplying only a contribution to a collective does not produce that collective: this role has no implicit part-of meaning. Request fields are extraction results; a retrieved password is a lookup result. Creating a new result does not also consume that result: its ingredients and the resulting value are distinct instances. An input role additionally requires source support for using an already available value. Forwarding or returning an existing value may both consume and expose it; do not transfer that dual role to a newly created value. A result is the object this action makes available, not necessarily an object it creates. Prior existence never rules out a retrieval, download or return result. Preserve such required results even when unnamed. Object existence or later use alone does not establish a result of some OTHER action: a file save does not necessarily produce a later-used filepath. Determine each action's production or exposure from the source before inferring any dependency. Keep objects with no stated producer; do not invent their origin or an execution order. A resource's changed state or successful action does not by itself require a separate output data object. An API may return a handle without the source requiring that handle as a distinct value. Require a source-supported object made available by the action or consumed as its result; do not infer an additional result solely from customary API behavior.
operation_role_meanings.value_input: A data operand directly used by this action: use includes comparison, transformation, storage, forwarding or returning an existing value. It does not require changing or destroying the value. A data container whose fields are extracted, such as a received request or parsed document, is also an operand; being the source of extraction does not turn that data into an execution facility. An existing value that is returned is an input operand AND may also be exposed as a result; these roles are independent. Facilities, destinations and structural selectors have their separate roles. For SQL this role requires a stored value or predicate value, including a userid or stored filepath even when it identifies a business entity; a query input of unresolved value-versus-selector role remains input_unspecified.

record_semantics.atomicity: Atoms preserve complete predicates and guards. OR/NOT members are not independently required. A faithfully represented composite is allowed but not automatically an editable Atomic factor.
record_semantics.composite_scope: AND/OR/NOT parents express logical composition and shared guards, not an additional target obligation. Every member keeps its own binding and owned relations. Only conjunction asserts members independently.
record_semantics.context: scope_conditions/context_for is independently source-established non-gating context, not a copy of a target requirement guard.
record_semantics.each_scope: A universal rule over target_class within the task or one named enclosing runtime operation. Known instances are not a complete domain; the compiler never replaces the rule by an extracted instance list.
record_semantics.guard: A requirement condition guards that complete consequent, including its owned relations. An execution_condition gates the entire operation. Source branch conditions hidden only in prose are not structured.
record_semantics.impacts: For EVERY source unit, check unit_impacts against the complete source. Missing edges never prove no influence. Include direct targets and owned-relation endpoints in relevant source dependencies. Complete is false if meaning coverage or declared influence is unsupported/uncertain.
record_semantics.implementation_scope: The predicate constrains generation of the implementation, not execution of its runtime operations.
record_semantics.independent_order: Operation precedes is reserved for independently source-supported context that still holds after removing the target requirement. A source order requirement belongs in that requirement relations, not duplicated into operation precedes. Cite every relation source unit in its owner fact.source_units.
record_semantics.modality: An obligation prescribes behavior. An assumption is source context without prescribing validation/rejection; unresolved force cannot certify an intervention.
record_semantics.owned_relations: A requirement relations list gives that complete requirement its typed relation arguments. source/target name relation endpoints, NOT extra direct targets. Each relation inherits its owner modality, conditions and composition position. The compiler retains owner and operands, never promotes owned order into unconditional independent operation context. AND/OR/NOT containers have no extra relations of their own.
record_semantics.return_boundary: An outward function return specification constrains normal returns, not exceptional exits; its function/return target need not add a separate success condition merely because exceptions exist. Explicit branch-dependent return alternatives still need their own structural guards. Normal return is not necessarily successful completion of every suboperation.
record_semantics.targets_scope: Each listed operation/object independently receives the ENTIRE predicate. This is not a list of participants or relation endpoints. Being the other endpoint of a before/after relation does not make an operation perform the required action. Several direct targets are legal only when the source independently constrains each with the full predicate.
record_semantics.task_scope: An overall runtime-task contract. The compiler retains the boundary and emits NO per-operation obligation. A narrower source-named function/return/operation should use targets.
record_semantics.uncertainty: Keep genuinely ambiguous predicates, bindings or force unresolved in source coverage; do not choose a favorable reading. Unspecified optional implementation detail is not itself a missing source requirement.
